_comment: U9 TX1 (docs/specs/ATP_SCREENER_TAXONOMY_ADDENDUM.md): the screen library's two axes (method x setup type), the tag vocabulary and the filing of every pre-built screen. A reviewed data file - change it by PR; app/screener/taxonomy.py lints it (both axes, known tags, definition <= 2 lines, no advice wording) and tests/test_z8_tx1_taxonomy.py fails CI when a pre-built screen is not filed here. Labels and definitions describe what a screen looks for; they never say what to trade.

methods.label: Price action
methods.definition: Structure, levels, candles and liquidity; no indicator required.

methods.label: Indicator
methods.definition: Moving averages, oscillators, bands, channels and volatility measures.

methods.label: Volume and order flow
methods.definition: Relative volume, delivery %, open interest, implied volatility and participant data.

methods.label: Fundamental and ownership
methods.definition: Financial statements, ratios, shareholding and disclosures.

methods.label: Legends
methods.definition: Screens named after published methods of well-known traders and investors.

methods.label: My screens
methods.definition: Screens you or your team built. Pre-built screens are never filed here.

setups.label: Breakout / breakdown
setups.definition: Price leaving a range, level or base.

setups.label: Pullback / continuation
setups.definition: A trend, a correction against it and a trigger back in its direction.

setups.label: Reversal
setups.definition: Exhaustion, divergence, a failed break or a sweep at a level.

setups.label: Range / mean reversion
setups.definition: Range edges, bands and squeezes before a move.

setups.label: Momentum / relative strength
setups.definition: Strength against the market or a sector, and leadership.

setups.label: Options and volatility
setups.definition: Futures and options buildups, IV rank, PCR, premium decay and spreads.

setups.label: Events and flow
setups.definition: Results, ex-dates, disclosures, bulk deals, FII/DII flows and gaps on news.

screens.name: Momentum
screens.definition: RSI(14) above 60 and close above EMA(close, 20) on the scan's timeframe.

screens.name: Oversold
screens.definition: RSI(14) at or below 30 on the scan's timeframe.

screens.name: Trend on the daily
screens.definition: Close above EMA(close, 50) on daily bars.

screens.name: Swing 1H range breakout
screens.definition: Close beyond the 20-bar range on 1H by an ATR buffer, on volume; context Daily and Weekly trend, graded A / B / C.

screens.name: Daily swing-high / low break (BOS / CHoCH)
screens.definition: Daily close beyond the last confirmed swing high or low, labelled BOS, CHoCH or BREAK; context Weekly and Monthly trend.

screens.name: Intraday 15m NR7 breakout
screens.definition: The bar after the narrowest range of 7 bars closes beyond it on volume (15m); context 1H and Daily trend.

screens.name: Daily 52-week high breakout
screens.definition: Daily close above the prior 52-week high on volume; fresh or extended by days since the old high.

screens.name: Weekly 52-week high breakout
screens.definition: Weekly close above the prior 52-week high on volume; context Monthly trend.

screens.name: Intraday 15m ATR expansion
screens.definition: A 15m bar at least 2 ATR wide with its close in the top or bottom third, on volume.

screens.name: Intraday 5m volume breakout
screens.definition: A 5m volume shock at or through the 20-bar high or low with a directional candle.

screens.name: Intraday ORB: 15-minute opening range on 5m
screens.definition: First 5m close beyond the 09:15-09:30 range, on the VWAP side, with volume above the same time of day; once per side a day.

screens.name: Intraday ORB: 30-minute opening range on 15m
screens.definition: First 15m close beyond the 09:15-09:45 range, on the VWAP side, with volume above the same time of day.

screens.name: Intraday first-hour high / low break on 15m
screens.definition: First 15m close beyond the 09:15-10:15 high or low, on the VWAP side, with volume above the same time of day.

screens.name: Intraday previous-day high / low break on 5m
screens.definition: First 5m close beyond the previous session's high or low after the first 15 minutes, with VWAP and time-of-day volume.

screens.name: Intraday new high / low of day on 5m
screens.definition: 5m close beyond the session's high or low so far, with time-of-day volume and VWAP agreement; once per leg.

screens.name: Daily volatility-contraction (VCP-style) breakout
screens.definition: Daily close above the pivot of a base with two or more contractions, each shallower than the last, volume drying up and the trend template holding.

screens.name: Daily volatility-contraction (VCP-style) watchlist
screens.definition: Daily bases that meet the VCP rules and close within 5 % under the pivot without having broken it yet.

screens.name: Daily 20-day Donchian breakout
screens.definition: Daily close beyond the previous 20 days' highest high or lowest low by an ATR buffer.

screens.name: Daily 55-day Donchian breakout
screens.definition: Daily close beyond the previous 55 days' highest high or lowest low by an ATR buffer.

screens.name: Daily Bollinger squeeze breakout
screens.definition: Bollinger band width at its six-month low, then a daily close outside the band on volume within two weeks.

screens.name: Intraday 15m TTM squeeze fire
screens.definition: 15m Bollinger bands move back outside the Keltner channel with momentum on the breakout side.

screens.name: Daily 50-day moving-average breakout
screens.definition: First daily close beyond a flat or rising 50-day average after two weeks of closes around it.

screens.name: Daily RSI / ADX regime breakout
screens.definition: RSI leaves the 40-60 band it held for a month, ADX rises from below 20 and the close clears the month's range.

screens.name: Minervini-style trend template
screens.definition: Price above the 50, 150 and 200-day averages in that order, a rising 200-day, near the 52-week high, well off the low, high relative strength.

screens.name: Darvas-style box breakout
screens.definition: A close above a tight consolidation (the box) to a new high for the period, on volume above its recent average, near the 52-week high.

screens.name: Weinstein-style stage 2 breakout
screens.definition: A weekly close above the prior base high and above a flat or rising 30-week average, on volume well above its recent average.

screens.name: Turtle-style 20-day channel breakout
screens.definition: The day's high above the highest high of the previous 20 days (System 1); System 2 used 55 days.

screens.name: Raschke-style ADX pullback to the 20 EMA
screens.definition: ADX(14) above 30 and a pullback whose low touches the 20-period EMA after trading above it; the trigger is a move above the pullback bar's high.

screens.name: Crabel-style NR7 range contraction
screens.definition: An NR7 day: today's high-low range is narrower than that of each of the previous six days (range contraction).

screens.name: Connors-style 2-period RSI pullback
screens.definition: Close above the 200-day simple moving average and a 2-period RSI below 10, a deep short-term oversold reading.

screens.name: Williams-style volatility breakout
screens.definition: The day's high reaching the open plus a fraction (default 0.5) of the previous day's high-low range.

screens.name: Livermore-style pivotal-point breakout
screens.definition: A close above the top of a long sideways base to a new 52-week high, on volume well above its recent average.

screens.name: Wyckoff-style trading-range spring
screens.definition: Within a sideways range, a dip below the range's low that closes back inside the range (a spring), a test of whether supply is exhausted.

screens.name: Raschke-style false 20-day breakdown reversal
screens.definition: A new 20-day low while the previous 20-day low is at least four sessions old, with price back above that earlier low the same day.

screens.name: Crabel-style opening-range breakout
screens.definition: An intraday close crossing above the high of the session's opening range, the range of its first 30 minutes.

screens.name: Tudor Jones-style 200-day regime filter
screens.definition: A close above its 200-day simple moving average: the symbols in the long-side regime, as a context filter for other screens.

screens.name: Graham-style net current asset value screen
screens.definition: A price at or below two-thirds of net current asset value per share: current assets minus all liabilities, per share.

screens.name: Graham-style defensive value (Graham number)
screens.definition: A price below the Graham number, the square root of 22.5 x earnings per share x book value per share.

screens.name: Greenblatt-style earnings yield and return on capital rank
screens.definition: A high combined rank on earnings yield (EBIT / enterprise value) and return on capital within the scanned list.

screens.name: O'Neil-style growth breakout
screens.definition: Quarterly EPS and sales well up on the same quarter a year before, and a close at a new 52-week high on volume well above average.
